the study of star formation and the interstellar medium in the Ophiuchis molecular cloud complex.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ophiuchis star formation is concentrated in the cluster, with a few small aggregates, but there are many isolated YSOs, and the star formation is still active.
the Ophiuchis clouds have been well surveyed in the near- to mid-infrared and are a rich source of information for the study of star formation.
the Spitzer Space telescope has revealed a rich, complex, and dynamic star-forming region in the Ophiuchis molecular cloud.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MIPS observations have detected the majority of the YSOs, both protostellar and pre–main-sequence stars, in the star-forming portions of the Ophiuchi clouds, and have revealed a large population of embedded YSOs in the non–star-formating portions of these clouds as well.
the star-forming regions of the Ophiucus dark clouds have been mapped with unprecedented sensitivity, revealing a wealth of information about the embedded protostellar populations.
Ophiuchus is a star-forming complex of clusters and aggregates, with a total mass of about 1000 M_⊙, that is surrounded by a more diffuse cloud of mass 2000–5000 M_⊦.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the star formation in Ophiuchus is not as spatially extended as previously thought.

the MIPS data reveal a rich population of YSOs that were previously hidden by their embedded nature, and that the YSOs are concentrated in clusters and aggregates that have been identified in previous work.
the MIPS observations of Ophiuchus are an invaluable tool in the study of the star formation history and evolution of this cloud complex.
